newsitem.title: UK: Safeway current same store sales up 3.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Safeway current same store sales up 3.2 pct.

text.p: British supermarket group Safeway Plc said on Tuesday that same store sales at its supermarkets were up 3.2 percent since the start of the current year.
In a statement to the annual meeting, chairman David Webster said prices were on average down 0.5 percent from last year, giving like-for-like volume sales in the period of "a healthy 3.7 percent".
Webster said total sales for the Safeway fascia were up 11 percent since the start of the year with total group sales up 7.3 percent, including Presto stores.

The current sales rise compares with figures released in May with annual results, which showed same store sales at Safeway up 3.7 percent with deflation of 0.9 percent in the first six weeks of the year.
"Our challenge remains, in the year ahead, to improve efficiency and grow volume sales," Webster said.
"Our industry continues to be highly competitive during a period of disinflation...and of increased revenue investment in customer service, technology based innovation and brand marketing," he added.
Safeway, behind market leader Tesco Plc and J. Sainsbury Plc in terms of market share, focuses on high-technology innovations for easing family shopping.

Tesco's latest current trading statement earlier this month showed same store sales up 5.1 percent while low-price ASDA said last week that same store sales jumped 9.2 percent in the year ending May 3.
